solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American city shedding last bright light

indicators.note: shedding its last means the final letter of the word for bright is dropped

parts.note: bright means clever, intelligent
to light on something is to land or come down on it, as a bird lights

explanation.surface: A US city is losing its last bright light, as if the power had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is a verb here: to alight or come down, as a bird does.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland is a major city in Ohio, in the United States.

clue.text: Band with heart of gold in Asian city

indicators.note: in tells us the central letters of gold go inside the word for band

parts.note: a combo is a small band of musicians, as in a jazz combo

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the two in the middle of gold

explanation.surface: A band with a heart of gold is playing in an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka, in South Asia.

clue.text: Philosopher lacking capital raised Australian native

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from the bottom up, reversed
lacking its capital means the philosopher's name loses its first letter

parts.note: David Hume was the Scottish philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher without money brought up a native Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking capital' takes H off HUME, leaving UME, and 'raised' turns that upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless bird found only in Australia, so a native there.

clue.text: Archdeacon lied, perhaps, after conclusion of divine service

indicators.note: after says the archdeacon and the song come behind the letter from divine
the conclusion of a word is its final letter, here the end of divine

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
a lied is a German art song, so an example of a song, signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: An archdeacon told a lie, perhaps, after the end of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like the past of lie, but it is the German word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Anglican Church, sung prayers at dusk.

clue.text: In dance they'd regularly taken steps

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words dance they'd, starting with the second

explanation.surface: In a dance, they had regularly taken steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To have taken steps is to have done something about a matter, that is, to have done the deed.

clue.text: Action involving sailors: Italian gets left

indicators.note: involving means the word for action wraps round the sailors and the Italian

parts.note: an action is a deed
POs are petty officers, naval sailors

explanation.surface: A naval action involving sailors in which an Italian is left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deposited has been put down and left in a place, like money left at a bank.

clue.text: Shy English class

parts.note: to shy is to throw, or cast

explanation.surface: Shy English people are described as a class of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective, but it is a verb meaning to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Commentators in play about God

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation meaning about
Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian god

explanation.surface: Pundits comment on a play about God.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek drama a group of performers stands apart and comments on the action of the play.

clue.text: Children entertaining grandpa arranged flowers

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a host would, so the word for children goes round the other letters

parts.note: sons are male children

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of grandpa are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The children entertain grandpa, who has arranged some flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' seems to describe a flower display, but it is grandpa's letters that get arranged (as NAPDRAG).
explanation.definitionFit: Snapdragons, or antirrhinums, are garden plants whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: Eastern king embracing no queen

indicators.note: embracing means the king's name holds the word no inside it

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king

explanation.surface: An Eastern king embraces nobody but no queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine was queen consort of France and later of England.

clue.text: Most flashy little boy grabbed by yahoo

indicators.note: grabbed by means the boy's name is held inside the word for yahoo

parts.note: a yahoo is a coarse brute, a lout
Des is a short form of the boy's name Desmond

explanation.surface: The flashiest little boy is grabbed by a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud can describe garish clothes or colours, so the superlative is the most flashy.

clue.text: Blasphemous academic again cut short

parts.note: prof, short for professor, is an academic

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word for again is dropped

parts.note: anew means again

explanation.surface: An academic, blasphemous again, is cut short mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane language shows irreverence towards sacred things, which is what blasphemy is.

clue.text: Grinders supplied by John Stuart's family

definitions.meaning: machines that grind corn or coffee, for example
John Stuart Mill, the philosopher, and his father James Mill

explanation.surface: Grinding machines supplied by a man called John Stuart's family firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn and pepper are ground in machines of this name, and John Stuart and James shared the surname.

clue.text: Rule is again broken in part of the Med

indicators.note: broken means the letters of rule is again are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rule is broken again in some Mediterranean region.
explanation.definitionFit: This arm of the Mediterranean lies off north-west Italy, by Genoa.

clue.text: Uproar about red bus breaking free

indicators.note: about means the word for uproar goes round the other letters

parts.note: din is a loud noise, uproar

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of red bus are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An uproar about a red bus breaking free of its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking free' reads as one phrase, but 'breaking' is the anagram signal (giving SBURDE) and 'free' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unburden or relieve someone of a load is to free them of it.

clue.text: Church feature recollected for a long time

indicators.note: recollected means the letters of for a long are gathered together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A church feature remembered for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered, but read as re-collected it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery in a church where the pipes and console of the instrument are housed.

clue.text: Fix it on beast like a mule

indicators.note: to fix can mean to rig or doctor, so the letters of it on beast are reworked

explanation.surface: Fix it on the beast, which is like a mule.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are proverbially stubborn, so the comparison describes someone refusing to budge.

clue.text: Just food, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means we want a word pronounced like the word for food

parts.note: fare is food, as in a menu's bill of fare

explanation.surface: Just food, by the sound of it, and nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: Being just means being fair and even-handed in judgment.

clue.text: Settle back in pantry with meat for dog

parts.note: to seal a deal is to settle it

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here the end of pantry

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Someone settles back in the pantry with meat for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle back' reads as a phrase for relaxing; split it: 'Settle' is SEAL and 'back in pantry' is the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham is a small white Welsh terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Soldier ready in Serbia

definitions.meaning: a paratrooper, a member of the Parachute Regiment
ready is slang for cash; a Serbian coin, a hundredth of a dinar

explanation.surface: A soldier is ready for action in Serbia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash, as in 'the readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratrooper is a soldier, and the Serbian dinar is divided into a hundred small coins of this name.

clue.text: Right to go through corridor

definitions.meaning: permission to travel across, as in safe conduct

explanation.surface: A right of way through a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's right of transit and an indoor hallway are both called by this word.

clue.text: Singular advantage before North African battle

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an edge is an advantage
a Moor is a North African, from the Maghreb

explanation.surface: A unique advantage held before a battle in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDGEMOOR is in Somerset, England: the last battle fought on English soil, in 1685.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Sedgemoor ended the Monmouth Rebellion against James II.

clue.text: Miserable missing wife may be gagged

indicators.note: missing means the word for miserable is without its letter for wife

parts.note: wretched means miserable

explanation.surface: A miserable man, missing his wife, may be silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gagged' suggests being silenced; here it means heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to heave as if about to vomit, which is the same as to retch.

clue.text: Munster county town wanting own wine

parts.note: Clare is a county in Munster, the south-western province of Ireland

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word town loses the letters of own

explanation.surface: A county town in Munster wants its own wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Inconsequential seconds and minutes never surpassed

parts.note: an all-time record is one never surpassed

explanation.surface: Seconds and minutes never surpassed seem unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time means minor or unimportant, as with a petty crook.

clue.text: Virgin from the south side of Detroit burst out

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means reading upward, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: pure means chaste, virgin

indicators.note: side of here takes the far end of Detroit, its last letter

explanation.surface: A virgin from the south side of Detroit has burst out.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that erupts bursts out in violent activity.

clue.text: Roll around unknown composer

indicators.note: around means the list goes round the unknown

parts.note: a roll is a list, as in a roll call
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, here Z

explanation.surface: A roll call around an unknown composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian pianist and composer of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Courts enclosing American land

indicators.note: enclosing means the word for courts wraps round the American

parts.note: atria are open courts within buildings

explanation.surface: Courtyards enclose an American's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a country in central Europe, and a land is a country.

clue.text: Free French article affected church

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
hit means affected badly, as in hit by the strike

explanation.surface: A free French article affected the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch a horse or trailer is to release it, setting it loose.

clue.text: Nip for nipper

explanation.surface: A small drink for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram of whisky and a toddler are both called by this short word.

clue.text: Outsiders ejected from Texan court? Just so!

indicators.note: with the outsiders ejected, only the inner letters of Texan remain

explanation.surface: Outsiders thrown out of a Texan court? Quite right!
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation the word agrees fully, meaning precisely or quite right.

clue.text: Head of Entertainment said I'm to enter ballpark

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Entertainment
to enter means the letters of I'm go inside the word for said

parts.note: stated means said

explanation.surface: The head of entertainment said he is to enter a baseball stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ballpark' reads as a stadium but is the adjective, as in a ballpark figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is a rough approximation, not an exact count.
